newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher as secondaries boost volumes.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher as secondaries boost volumes.

text.p: The surge of secondary stocks boosted the market to a higher close with punters dominating trading activities, dealers said.
Fifteen of the top 20 most active stocks hit new highs for the year. Total volume stood at 380 million shares.

Dealers said a mixture of pure speculation and rumours of restructuring drove many of the active stocks. "This is madness. It's a very manipulative market," said Victor Wan, senior analyst at South Johore Securities.
The Second Board index ended at 607.13, up 8.74 points or 1.46 percent, after hitting a record intraday high of 613.00.
Blue chips were lukewarm, with the Composite Index notching a 2.87 point gain to 1,130.60.

Top active Innovest was suspended at midday after rising 60 cents to 10.50 ringgit, just below a new year high of 10.60. Dealers said rumours of restructuring and new project injections helped the stock.
Other active stocks driven by restructuring rumours include Rashid Hussain and Aokam, which were up 50 and 10 cents respectively.
Renong, which reported strong full-year earnings on Thursday, ended down two cents to 3.84 after an initial run.
